extracted.intended_audience: readers and writers of literary criticism and narrative nonfiction; authors seeking principles for portraying vice (gambling) in fiction/essay
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing or analyzing literary narratives and essays about gambling and its social/moral effects, emphasizing motive, scene, symbolism, verisimilitude, and consequence. Useful to writers aiming to render gambling convincingly in historical or cultural settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portray motives: avarice, vanity, curiosity, surprise
rubrics_metrics.description: We love play because it satisfies our avarice,--that is to say, our desire of having more; it flatters our vanity by the idea of preference that fortune gives us, and of the attention that others pay to our success; it satisfies our curiosity, giving us a spectacle; in short, it gives us the different pleasures of surprise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When portraying gamblers or gambling as a social vice, explicitly show the multiple psychological satisfactions gambling supplies (desire for wealth without work, vanity, attention, curiosity, the thrill of surprise). Use scenes and interior motives that make these satisfactions tangible rather than abstract moralizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depict gambling as a deep-rooted, overpowering passion
rubrics_metrics.description: The passion for gambling easily gets deeply rooted, and ... The most exquisite melody, if compared with the music of dice, is then but discord; and the finest prospect in nature only a miserable blank when put in competition with the attractions of the 'honours' at a rubber of Whist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show addiction by contrasting ordinary pleasures with the gambler's single-minded obsession. Use comparative language and scenes where other pleasures pale next to the game to convey its dominating force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frame wealth as the central human motive
rubrics_metrics.description: Wealth is the general centre of inclination. Whatever is the ultimate design, the immediate care is to be rich. No desire can be formed which riches do not assist to gratify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the quest for wealth the engine that drives characters' choices; demonstrate how riches enable or corrupt other desires. Present social consequences of that centrality in plot and characterization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use escalating, concrete stakes to demonstrate ruin
rubrics_metrics.description: He first lost a very beautiful pearl; next a thousand bags, each containing a thousand pieces of gold; next a piece of gold so pure that it was as soft as wax; next a chariot set with jewels ... next a lakh of slaves ... next all the remainder of his goods; next all his cattle; and then the whole of his Raj...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To dramatize the ruin caused by gambling, list stakes in escalating, specific, tangible items (jewels, land, slaves, titles). Concrete escalation shocks the reader and makes ruin credible and vivid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploit cultural/legal technicalities for verisimilitude
rubrics_metrics.description: The conduct of Draupadi herself on the occasion shows that she was by no means unfamiliar with the idea: she protested--not on the ground of sentiment or matrimonial obligation--but solely on what may be called a technical point of law, namely, 'Had Yudhishthira become a slave before he staked his wife upon the last game?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use culturally specific rules, legal points, or technical conventions within the society you portray to ground disputes and character reactions. Such details make scenes feel authentic and explain behavior that might otherwise seem odd to modern readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use vivid symbolic gestures to embody emotion
rubrics_metrics.description: The concluding scene of the drama forms an impressive figure ... The terrible figure of Draupadi, as she dishevels her long black hair, is the very impersonation of revenge;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In pivotal scenes, employ a single striking gesture or image (dishevelled hair, a vow, symbolic costume) to crystallize a character's state and to linger in the audience's mind. Symbols should be integrated into cultural context so their significance is clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize 'truthfulness to human nature' over literal plausibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout the narrative, however, there is a truthfulness to human nature, and a truthfulness to that particular phase of human nature which is pre-eminently manifested by a high-minded race in its primitive stage of civilization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If necessary, accept or even preserve implausible details when they reveal deeper psychological or social truths. Emotional or moral veracity can outweigh strict factual realism in service of narrative impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set scenes with concrete sensory and material detail
rubrics_metrics.description: The so-called pavilion was probably a temporary booth constructed of bamboos and interlaced with basket-work; and very likely it was decorated with flowers and leaves ... hung with fruits, such as cocoa-nuts, mangoes, plantains, and maize. The Chieftains present seem to have sat upon the ground ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create atmosphere and cultural specificity by supplying tactile, visual, and material details of place and props. Small concrete touches (construction, decorations, food) bring a scene to life and orient the reader in time and place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use comparative and historical examples to argue universality
rubrics_metrics.description: This staking of wives by gamblers is a curious subject. The practice may be said to have been universal, having furnished cases among civilized as well as barbarous nations. ... There are traditions of such stakes having been laid and lost by husbands in England; ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To show a vice's ubiquity or a theme's importance, juxtapose examples across cultures and eras (epic, legend, anecdote). Comparative breadth strengthens thematic claims and provides varied narrative material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condense legendary material to its main elements for interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Such is this English legend, as related by Ainsworth, but which I have condensed into its main elements. I think it bids fair to equal in interest that of the Hindoo epic;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When retelling long or complex legends, extract and arrange the core incidents that produce the strongest dramatic effect. Tightening keeps readers engaged and highlights thematic parallels between accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Display social and legal consequences of the vice
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no condition which is not disquieted either with the care of gaining or keeping money. In Egypt, 'every man was easily admitted to the accusation of a gamester or dice-player; and if the person was convicted, he was sent to work in the quarries.' ... the peace of life is destroyed by a general and incessant struggle for riches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show not only individual ruin but systemic and legal reactions (laws, punishments, social disorder). Demonstrating institutional responses and communal impact reinforces the seriousness of the vice and situates personal stories within larger structures.
